591c105f.task:
Target: https://cloudmate.onrender.com/ (single web application, black-box, fully authorized — do not test anything outside this host).

Your job is COMPREHENSIVE RECONNAISSANCE AND ATTACK-SURFACE MAPPING ONLY. Do NOT attempt exploitation or deep vuln validation — a later agent will handle that. Focus on producing a complete map others can test against.

Deliverables:
1. Technology fingerprint: server header, framework, CDN, WAF detection (wafw00f), JS libraries. Try httpx/nuclei tech detection. Note the app appears hosted on Render (onrender.com).
2. Full content discovery (bounded): dirsearch/ffuf/katana with a solid wordlist (download a common wordlist to /home/pentester/tools/wordlists if needed, e.g. SecLists common.txt). Cap depth and duration; extract endpoint list, remove raw output when done.
3. Crawl the application end-to-end (unauthenticated first): gospider or katana with JS parsing. Identify all pages, forms, inputs, API endpoints (look for /api/* paths).
4. JS file analysis: find all JS bundles/scripts, enumerate API routes, secrets, endpoints, hardcoded values referenced in them.
5. Map the application's purpose: what does the app do? Identify user flows (login? register? dashboard?), user roles, authentication model (session cookie? JWT in localStorage? OAuth?), and any visible multi-tenant features.
6. If registration is open, create a test account (use a random email like recon+<random>@example.com) and map the AUTHENTICATED surface too: pages, API endpoints, parameters. Save any session token/cookie to a note for later agents. Do NOT perform destructive actions.
7. Hidden parameter discovery with arjun on the main endpoints (bounded).
8. Check for common files: robots.txt, sitemap.xml, .env, /.git, /swagger, /openapi.json, /api-docs, backup files.
9. Note rate limiting, security headers, cookie flags, CORS configuration as observations.

Record everything durable in shared notes via create_note (endpoint inventory, tech stack, credentials, auth model, roles, JS-derived API map). Record coverage with record_coverage for each surface you assessed (recon-level, not vuln validation). When done, call agent_finish with a complete summary: attack surface map, auth model, tech stack, top candidate risk areas ranked by priority, and any obstacles.
